theory.intro: Once alcohol consumption stops, the liver breaks down alcohol at a steady average rate of $0.015\text{ g}/100\text{ mL}$ of blood per hour. The time required for blood alcohol content (**BAC**) to decrease to zero is calculated using $\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$.
facts: $\text{Time (hours)} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$, where $\text{BAC}$ is the blood alcohol content when drinking stops.
The constant $0.015$ is the hourly rate of alcohol clearance from the bloodstream ($0.015\text{ g}/100\text{ mL/h}$).
To convert decimal hours to hours and minutes, multiply the decimal portion by $60$ minutes.
Learner and provisional drivers require a BAC of exactly $0.00$ to drive legally.
Passing time is the only way BAC decreases; sleep, coffee, showers, and food do not accelerate liver metabolism.
steps: Substitute the BAC into the time formula
Convert decimal hours to hours and minutes if required

foundation.question_text: A person has a BAC of $0.045$. Use $\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$ to calculate the number of hours required for their BAC to reach zero.
A driver has a BAC of $0.06$. Calculate the time in hours needed for their BAC to drop to zero.
A person records a BAC of $0.075$. Find the time in hours for their BAC to drop to zero.
A person has a BAC of $0.05$. Calculate the time required for their BAC to reach zero, in hours and minutes.
A person has a BAC of $0.08$. Calculate the time required for their BAC to reach zero, in hours and minutes.
A driver finishes drinking at $11{:}00\text{ pm}$ with a BAC of $0.045$. At what clock time will their BAC reach zero?
It takes $6\text{ hours}$ for a person's BAC to return to zero. What was their BAC when they stopped drinking?

development.question_text: A person has a BAC of $0.038$. Calculate the time, in hours and minutes (rounded to the nearest minute), for their BAC to decrease to zero.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$
$= \dfrac{0.038}{0.015}$
$= 2.533\ldots\text{ hours}$
$= 2\text{ hours and } (0.533\ldots \times 60)\text{ minutes}$
$= 2\text{ hours } 32\text{ minutes}$

development.question_text: An individual has a BAC of $0.094$. Calculate the time, in hours and minutes (to the nearest minute), needed to reach zero BAC.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$
$= \dfrac{0.094}{0.015}$
$= 6.266\ldots\text{ hours}$
$= 6\text{ hours and } (0.266\ldots \times 60)\text{ minutes}$
$= 6\text{ hours } 16\text{ minutes}$

development.question_text: A person stops drinking at $1{:}30\text{ am}$ with a BAC of $0.055$. At what clock time the following morning will their BAC reach zero? Answer to the nearest minute.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Time} = \dfrac{0.055}{0.015}$
$= 3.666\ldots\text{ hours}$
$= 3\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$
$1{:}30\text{ am} + 3\text{ h } 40\text{ min} = 5{:}10\text{ am}$

development.question_text: Chloe stops drinking at $10{:}45\text{ pm}$ on Friday with a BAC of $0.072$. Find the earliest time on Saturday morning that she can legally drive on a Provisional licence ($0.00$ BAC limit).
development.solution_text:
$\text{Time} = \dfrac{0.072}{0.015}$
$= 4.8\text{ hours}$
$= 4\text{ hours } 48\text{ minutes}$
$10{:}45\text{ pm} + 4\text{ h } 48\text{ min} = 3{:}33\text{ am}$

development.question_text: Mark ($80\text{ kg}$ male) consumes $6$ standard drinks over $3\text{ hours}$. Use $\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$ and $\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$ to calculate how many hours and minutes he must wait after drinking stops to reach zero BAC. Round to the nearest minute.

Jessica ($54\text{ kg}$ female) consumes $4$ standard drinks over $2\text{ hours}$. Calculate the waiting time after drinking stops for her BAC to reach zero, in hours and minutes to the nearest minute.

A driver who stopped drinking at midnight was tested at $5{:}00\text{ am}$ and found to have a BAC of exactly $0.00$. If their BAC took exactly $4\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$ to reach zero, calculate their BAC at midnight to 3 decimal places.

mastery.question_text: Aaron is a $72\text{ kg}$ male P-plate driver. He consumes $5$ standard drinks between $8{:}00\text{ pm}$ and $11{:}30\text{ pm}$ ($3.5\text{ hours}$). Calculate his estimated BAC at $11{:}30\text{ pm}$ and determine the earliest time the next morning he can legally drive his car (zero BAC limit).
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10(5) - 7.5(3.5)}{6.8(72)} = \dfrac{23.75}{489.6} \approx 0.04851$
$\text{Time} = \dfrac{0.04851}{0.015} \approx 3.234\text{ hours} = 3\text{ hours } 14\text{ minutes}$
$11{:}30\text{ pm} + 3\text{ h } 14\text{ min} = 2{:}44\text{ am}$

mastery.question_text: A $60\text{ kg}$ female attends a party from $7{:}00\text{ pm}$ to $11{:}00\text{ pm}$ and consumes $4$ standard drinks. She needs to drive to work at $6{:}00\text{ am}$ the next morning as a Provisional driver ($0.00$ limit). Determine by calculation whether she will reach zero BAC before $6{:}00\text{ am}$, and find her BAC at $6{:}00\text{ am}$.
mastery.solution_text:
At $11{:}00\text{ pm}$:
$\text{BAC} = \dfrac{10(4) - 7.5(4)}{5.5(60)} = \dfrac{10}{330} \approx 0.0303$
$\text{Time to zero} = \dfrac{0.0303}{0.015} \approx 2.02\text{ hours} = 2\text{ hours } 1\text{ minute}$
$11{:}00\text{ pm} + 2\text{ h } 1\text{ min} = 1{:}01\text{ am}$
Since $1{:}01\text{ am}$ is well before $6{:}00\text{ am}$, her BAC will be $0.00$ and she can legally drive.

mastery.question_text: Toby ($88\text{ kg}$ male, $7$ drinks in $4\text{ hours}$) and Hannah ($56\text{ kg}$ female, $5$ drinks in $4\text{ hours}$) both stop drinking at $1{:}00\text{ am}$. Calculate how many minutes longer Toby must wait than Hannah for his BAC to drop to zero, rounded to the nearest minute.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{BAC}_{\text{Toby}} = \dfrac{10(7) - 7.5(4)}{6.8(88)} = \dfrac{40}{598.4} \approx 0.06685$
$\text{Time}_{\text{Toby}} = \dfrac{0.06685}{0.015} \approx 4.4563\text{ h} \approx 267.4\text{ min}$
$\text{BAC}_{\text{Hannah}} = \dfrac{10(5) - 7.5(4)}{5.5(56)} = \dfrac{20}{308} \approx 0.06494$
$\text{Time}_{\text{Hannah}} = \dfrac{0.06494}{0.015} \approx 4.3290\text{ h} \approx 259.7\text{ min}$
$\text{Difference} = 267.4 - 259.7 = 7.7\text{ min} \approx 8\text{ minutes}$
